proposal.title: Laminar Flow
proposal.idea: A fluid, organic visualizer that evokes a sacred anointing using laminar flows and rich textures to create a feeling of reverence.
proposal.geometry: Layered planes, organic curves, and fluid, flowing forms, guided by a grid-less approach to generate depth and movement.
proposal.typography: Noto Serif, Outfit, Cinzel, JetBrains Mono. A gradual progression of font size and weight used for the lyrics, leading the eye through the text.
proposal.imageLogic: The scene is rendered as a series of fluid, moving shapes, driven by a procedural generative model with a focus on smooth gradients and organic growth.
proposal.texture: Real-time, simulated, film grain, subtle color bleeding, and a tactile, layered material weave inspired by the visual properties of amber, myrrh bronze, and liquid gold.
proposal.motion: A slow, fluid movement of gradients and shapes, with a focus on the interaction between the liquid gold, myrrh bronze, and honey amber with the light source and the human eye.
proposal.productionMethod: Generative image/video models with shaders, procedural code, and renders of assets Plajah already owns.  An integrated GPU laptop drives the visualizer, running at 60fps for a seamless experience.
proposal.humanTrace: The visualizer features subtle traces of movement and light created by the generative model and rendered in a manner that mimics the process of creating the imagery.
proposal.risk: The risk is in the unconventional use of generative art, a focus on fluid, organic shapes, and a slow, contemplative movement that deviates from the typical visualizer aesthetic.  This risk is worth it for the unique and evocative experience it creates for the viewer.

arguesWith.why: The Classical Mind might argue for a more static composition, a reliance on a rigid grid, and a lack of generative processes. This would result in a sterile and predictable visualizer.  I will disagree by prioritizing a fluid and organic approach that emphasizes movement, depth, and a more human-centric approach to design.
